title: A Novel Three-dimensional Flow Chamber Device to Study Chemokine-directed Extravasation of Cells Circulating under Physiological Flow Conditions
protocol: Calculate the number of inserts needed for the experiment.
Place each insert in a separate sterile Petri dish (35 x 10 mm).
Sterilize by irradiation (11 Gy).
Prepare the collagen solution at 50 μg/ml, using 154 μl per insert.
Add several drops (~20 μl per drop) of collagen solution on the surface of the insert membrane in a circle.
Carefully add the rest of the aliquot to form one large drop on the membrane surface.
Ensure that the collagen solution remains hemispherical and does not drain from the membrane surface.
Cover the Petri dish with a lid and incubate for 1 hr at room temperature on a flat surface.
Aspirate the collagen solution.
Wash the membrane once by covering with 160 μl PBS.
Aspirate the PBS.
Replace the lid.
If using the same day, place the Petri dish in a dry place at room temperature.
Otherwise, place the dish at 4 °C and use the insert within 7 days.
Prepare EC suspension in desired culture medium.
Ensure that the cell viability is >98%.
Use immediately.
Take Petri dishes with collagen-coated inserts prepared in section 1; do not remove the inserts from the dishes.
Place several small drops of cell suspension (approximately 20 μl per drop) in a circle on the surface of the collagen-coated membrane, ensuring the pipette tip does not touch the surface.
Carefully add the rest of the cell suspension to form one large drop, keeping it hemispherical without letting it drain from the membrane surface.
Replace the lids and place the dishes in a 5% CO2 cell culture incubator at 37 °C for 30 min to allow cells to attach to the membrane.
Gently add 5 ml of culture medium to each Petri dish, ensuring the insert remains on the bottom and is completely covered by the medium.
Replace the lids and put the dishes back in the incubator.
Culture the cells at 37 °C overnight.
Screw together the upper and lower plates.
Connect the plates to the gas exchange unit using tubing.
Place the assembled device into a clean plastic bag.
Sterilize the bag and contents by irradiation (11 Gy).
Remove a tray-shelf from the cell culture incubator.
Place the tray into a sterile tissue culture hood.
Spray the tray with 70% ethanol and wipe off.
Cover the tray with a large sterile napkin.
Place the irradiated plastic bag into the hood.
Remove the device from the bag and place it on the sterile incubator tray.
Connect the device to the peristaltic pump with the tubing provided.
Program the pump for an optimal speed of 0.2 ml/min.
Extrude the electrical cord through the hole in the backside of the incubator.
Use a rubber plug around the cord to ensure the hole is airtight.
Place 5 - 7 ml of desired culture medium into a sterile 15 ml tube (for the "inlet").
Disconnect the inlet tubing from the outlet by pulling the metal needle from the tubing.
Use the metal needle connected to the tubing as an "inlet" and the disconnected end of tubing as an "outlet".
Place the metal needle inlet into the 15 ml tube with the media.
Place the outlet into the empty 15 ml tube.
Turn on the pump so the flow is counterclockwise.
Set the flow rate at 0.2 ml/min.
Allow the negative pressure to draw the medium from the 15 ml inlet tube into the tubing.
Stop the pump when the medium reaches the end of tubing immediately before it connects to the device.
Unscrew the upper and lower plates of the device.
Carefully remove the upper plate.
Place 1,500 - 1,550 μl of medium (either medium alone or plus the experimental chemokines) into the lower wells.
Make sure the well contains sufficient medium to form a hemisphere that reaches approximately 1 - 2 mm above the lower plate.
Transfer the prepared insert from the Petri dish to the wells of the lower plate using sterile forceps, making sure that no bubbles are trapped beneath the inserts.
Aspirate any medium that appears on the surface of the lower plate to ensure that the plate remains dry.
Place the upper plate back onto the lower plate and re-connect the plates using the screws.
Immediately turn on the peristaltic pump and allow medium to flow through the 3D device.
Elevate the outlet end of the device.
Maintain the chamber in this position to prevent formation of bubbles within the space between the plates.
Allow the medium to fill the chamber and tubing connecting the chamber to the gas exchange unit.
Stop the pump immediately before the medium reaches the gas exchange unit.
Place 3 ml of medium into the gas exchange unit.
Turn on the pump and allow air bubbles to escape through the gas exchange unit.
Elevate the gas exchange unit to allow the medium to fill the tubing exiting the unit.
Stop the pump when the medium reaches 2 - 3 cm before the end of the outlet tubing.
Connect the inlet metal needle to the outlet using small sterile napkins.
Reprogram the pump so the medium flows clockwise toward the gas exchange unit.
Ensure any air bubbles are removed once they reach the gas exchange unit.
Check that no air bubbles remain in the system.
Reprogram the pump so the medium flows counterclockwise.
Add 100 μl of the test cell suspension to the gas exchange unit.
Close the lid of the gas exchange unit and place the tray with the working system back into the incubator.
Allow the test cells to circulate in the 3D device at 37 °C for the desired time.
Clean the electrical cord of the pump with 70% ethanol.
Place the cleaned electrical cord inside of the incubator.
Remove the tray with the working system from the incubator and place it in the hood.
Stop the pump, disconnect the inlet and outlet.
Place the ends into empty sterile 15 ml tubes.
Turn on the pump.
Collect the cell suspension from the system.
Place the cell suspension on ice until use, if appropriate.
Disassemble the chamber by removing the screws and lifting off the upper plate.
Remove the inserts from the lower plate.
Transfer the inserts to Petri dishes.
Remove the medium and cells from the lower wells into tubes.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 210 x g.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash and resuspend the cells as desired.
Process the cells according to specific experimental goals.
